resources.string: Package Manager
Core patches for app installation and updates
Enable Core Patch
Choose the checks to relax below. Turning this off restores the original checks for new installs and keeps your selections.
Core patches
Additional install options
Install an older app version
Install an older version over the current one without uninstalling it first.
Install a re-signed update
Replace a regular app with an APK signed by someone else. The replacement can read the existing app data.
Allow v1-only signatures
Install an APK with a v1 signature when Android requires v2 or newer.
Allow modified APK contents
Install an APK whose files changed after signing. The APK still needs readable signing certificates.
Allow mismatched split signatures
Install a base APK and its language, device or feature splits together even when their signers differ.
Allow mismatched signatures in a shared UID
Some apps use a shared Android identity to access the same data. Allow regular apps to join such a group with a different signature.
Allow apps built for older Android versions
Use when Android rejects an app because it targets an Android version that is too old.
Allow compressed resource tables
Use when Android rejects an APK because resources.arsc is compressed or misaligned.
Skip the package verification agent
Skip the separate service Android asks to verify an install. APK signature checks have their own switches above.
Allow updates to persistent apps
Use when Android rejects an update because the app is marked as always running.
Allow blocked HyperOS system app updates
Skip the HyperOS rule that prevents certain system app updates. Android still checks the system app signature.
Skip HyperOS install isolation
Use when HyperOS blocks an APK based on where it came from or on device rules declared by the APK.
